text: In IS1006b, what device scope was agreed for the initial release of the remote?
reference_answer: Televisions only, with a more general-purpose remote left as a possible later extension.
author: gm

text: In IS1009d, what materials were specified for the case and the buttons?
reference_answer: A plastic case and soft rubber buttons.
author: gm

text: In TS3011a, who was expected to buy the remote, and where would they buy it?
reference_answer: Individual consumers buying it in retail stores.
author: gm

text: In IS1006a, which users was the remote's adaptable layout intended to accommodate?
reference_answer: Both left-handed and right-handed users.
author: gm

text: What colour was specified for the LED in IS1009d?
reference_answer: Fluorescent green.
author: gm

text: In IS1008d, where was the microphone to be placed so it could be used with the flap closed?
reference_answer: On the side of the remote, where it could pick up speech with the flap closed.
author: gm

text: What control was agreed for changing channels and adjusting volume in TS3011b?
reference_answer: A single round button that could be pressed in four directions.
author: gm

text: In ES2008b, did the team restrict the target audience to a fixed age range?
reference_answer: No. It chose to focus on simplicity and fashion across a broad range of ages.
author: gm

text: In TS3005c, how was the touchscreen intended to be operated, and was a stylus to be supplied?
reference_answer: The touchscreen was to be operated with fingers, without a stylus.
author: gm

text: What selling price was specified for the remote in IS1003a?
reference_answer: 25 euros.
author: gm

text: Which company slogan was to be incorporated into the remote's design in ES2016b?
reference_answer: "We put the fashion in electronics."
author: gm

text: How was a multi-digit channel number to be entered in the ES2014b design?
reference_answer: Using the 0–9 digit buttons in sequence, with a delay that allows successive presses to form a multi-digit channel number.
author: gm

text: What protection against water did the team agree the remote should have in TS3003a?
reference_answer: The remote should be waterproof.
author: gm

text: In TS3011b, what was the purpose of the 'dual channel watch' button?
reference_answer: To switch back and forth between two selected television channels using one button.
author: gm

text: In IS1006c, how would opting for additional LCD colours affect the price paid by the user?
reference_answer: The user would pay extra for the additional screen colours.
author: gm

text: What was decided about teletext in IS1006b?
reference_answer: Teletext was to be excluded.
author: gm

text: How were the buttons to be labelled in IS1009d?
reference_answer: The numeric channel buttons would carry numbers, while the other buttons would carry recognisable symbols.
author: gm

text: How was the size of the wooden case to be customised in IS1008c?
reference_answer: The size would be tailored to the user's hand, for example by making the remote wider for larger hands.
author: gm

text: How was the kinetic battery in the ES2008c design intended to recharge?
reference_answer: Through movement of the remote, such as pressing its buttons.
author: gm

text: What automatic behaviour after inactivity was planned for the remote in TS3005b?
reference_answer: It would enter standby automatically after roughly two to three minutes without use.
author: gm

text: What did the team decide about including an LCD screen in TS3011c?
reference_answer: Not to include an LCD screen in the remote.
author: gm

text: Which age group was chosen as the target audience in ES2002b?
reference_answer: People aged 15 to 35.
author: gm

text: What overall shape was agreed for the remote in ES2002c?
reference_answer: A snowman-like shape, with a larger section held in the hand and a smaller rounded section above it.
author: gm

text: What size-adjustment option for the on-screen buttons was agreed in TS3005b?
reference_answer: Allow the on-screen buttons to be enlarged.
author: gm

text: Which fruit shape was officially agreed for the standby button in ES2014d?
reference_answer: A cherry.
author: gm

text: For the cost-adjusted design agreed in IS1003d, which material is selected for the remote control case?
reference_answer: Plastic, replacing the wood selected in IS1003c.
author: gm

text: For the cost-adjusted design agreed in IS1003d, how many solar cells are retained?
reference_answer: One solar cell.
author: gm

text: What company logo and placement are selected for the remote control by the end of IS1003d?
reference_answer: The double-R company logo is to be integrated on one side of the remote control.
author: gm

text: At the close of ES2016d, how many batteries are selected for the remote control?
reference_answer: Two batteries.
author: gm

text: At the close of ES2016d, what type of scrolling control is retained in the design?
reference_answer: An iPod-style scroll wheel.
author: gm

text: What information is the LCD intended to provide in the design agreed by the end of TS3003d?
reference_answer: Channel numbers during scrolling, plus instructions for using the scroll wheel and other buttons, such as the subtitles control.
author: gm

text: Which colour variants of the remote must carry the RR logo under the final agreement in ES2008d?
reference_answer: All colour variants must carry the RR logo, not just the version in company colours.
author: gm

text: What requirement applies to the use of company colours across the product variants agreed in ES2008d?
reference_answer: At least one variant must use the company's corporate colour scheme.
author: gm

text: Is speech recognition retained in the final design agreed in TS3005d?
reference_answer: No. Speech recognition is removed during the cost review.
author: gm

text: What shape is selected for the volume buttons in the final ES2014d design?
reference_answer: Lemon-shaped buttons.
author: gm

text: What colour is selected for the buttons on the hidden panel in ES2014d, including the Enter button?
reference_answer: All of them are standard blue, including Enter.
author: gm

text: In the general layout retained for IS1008d, where are the volume and channel controls positioned relative to the numeric keypad?
reference_answer: Volume and channel controls are placed for thumb access, while the less frequently used numeric keypad is lower down.
author: gm

text: What power source is retained in the final design agreed in ES2014d?
reference_answer: Kinetic power generated by movement of the remote control.
author: gm

text: What chip type is specified in the final ES2014d design?
reference_answer: A simple chip.
author: gm

text: After the cost reductions in TS3005d, what curvature is retained for the case?
reference_answer: A single curve.
author: gm

text: What chip-on-print type is retained in the final ES2016d design?
reference_answer: An advanced chip-on-print.
author: gm

text: After the budget adjustments in TS3005d, what material remains specified for the remote's case?
reference_answer: Rubber.
author: gm

text: After the budget adjustments in TS3005d, which chip type remains in the design?
reference_answer: An advanced chip-on-print.
author: gm

text: What case curvature is retained in the final ES2014d design?
reference_answer: A single curve.
author: gm

text: What is the case's main material in the final ES2016d design?
reference_answer: Plastic.
author: gm

text: After the cost adjustments in TS3005d, what power source remains in the design?
reference_answer: Battery power.
author: gm

text: After comparing flat and curved cases in TS3003d, what case curvature does the team retain?
reference_answer: A single curve.
author: gm

text: What power source remains in the final ES2002d design after the cost review?
reference_answer: Battery power, with the kinetic source removed.
author: gm

text: In the final ES2002d design, where is navigation feedback shown?
reference_answer: On the television screen, with no LCD on the remote.
author: gm

text: What case material is chosen for the prototype costed in TS3003d?
reference_answer: Plastic.
author: gm

text: How did the case-material decision change from IS1003c to IS1003d, and why?
reference_answer: In IS1003c the team selected wood. In IS1003d it replaced wood with plastic to meet the EUR 12.50 production-cost limit. Plastic was described as free in the costing discussion.
author: gm
superseded_answer: A wooden case is selected for the remote control.

text: How was the solar-power decision refined from IS1003c to IS1003d, and why was that refinement made?
reference_answer: In IS1003c the team adopted solar energy together with batteries. In IS1003d it specified a single solar cell to limit production costs, after identifying solar cells as too expensive.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The remote control is to use solar energy together with batteries.

text: How was the corporate-branding requirement refined between IS1003b and IS1003d, and what prompted the final logo decision?
reference_answer: In IS1003b the team required Real Reaction's corporate image to be recognizable through colour and slogan. In IS1003d it noticed that the logo was still missing and agreed to place the double R on one side to fulfil that outstanding branding requirement.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Real Reaction's corporate image should be recognizable through the remote control's colour and slogan.

text: How was the battery decision refined from ES2016c to ES2016d, and why was that quantity selected?
reference_answer: In ES2016c the team selected conventional batteries as the power source. In ES2016d it fixed the quantity at two, rejecting four because they would make the remote too heavy.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The remote control is to use conventional batteries.

text: How was the scrolling-function decision refined from ES2016b to ES2016c, and why did the chosen mechanism require a more expensive chip?
reference_answer: ES2016b called for a scrolling function. In ES2016c the team chose an iPod-style scrolling control for its simple menu interface and accepted a more sophisticated, more expensive chip-on-print because that mechanism required it.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The remote control should include a scrolling function.

text: How did the intended role of the LCD develop from TS3003b to TS3003d, and why was it retained during the redesign?
reference_answer: In TS3003b a small screen was selected to explain button functions when pressed. In TS3003d it also shows channel numbers during scrolling and helps users operate the scroll wheel and other buttons. Replacing the number buttons with a scroll wheel saves money, allowing the LCD to be kept to provide help for the redesigned controls.
author: gm
superseded_answer: A small LCD screen explains what a button does when it is pressed.

text: How was the branding requirement in ES2008b made more specific in ES2008d, and what omission did the team address?
reference_answer: ES2008b required a recognisable corporate image through the company's colours and slogan. In ES2008d the team noticed that logo provision had not been addressed and explicitly required the RR logo on every colour variant, rather than only the concept in company colours.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The design must make the corporate image recognisable through company colours and the slogan.

text: How did the planned colour range develop from ES2008c to ES2008d, and why was a version in company colours added?
reference_answer: In ES2008c the team chose colours inspired by fruit and vegetables. In ES2008d it added a version using company colours alongside the other colour concepts, after noticing that the requirement to use company colours had been overlooked.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The remote should be offered in colours inspired by fruit and vegetables.

text: How did the plan for a microphone supporting speech recognition change from TS3005c to TS3005d, and why?
reference_answer: In TS3005c a microphone was planned for speech recognition if that feature was implemented. In TS3005d the team dropped speech recognition and removed its microphone and speaker to reduce production costs.
author: gm
superseded_answer: A microphone is planned for speech recognition if that feature is implemented.

text: How did the design of the volume controls develop from ES2014b to ES2014d, and what purpose did the final shape serve?
reference_answer: In ES2014b the front interface was assigned volume-up and volume-down controls. In ES2014d the team chose lemon-shaped volume buttons so they would stand out while keeping a fruit theme in the design.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The front interface includes volume-up and volume-down controls.

text: How was the hidden-panel design specified more precisely from ES2014b to ES2014d, and why were different button colours judged unnecessary?
reference_answer: In ES2014b the hidden panel was assigned brightness, contrast, channel-tuning and Enter controls. In ES2014d all its buttons were specified as standard blue, including Enter. Extra colours were judged unnecessary because users examine that panel more deliberately, and the unused allowance was kept as profit.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The hidden panel contains controls for brightness, contrast and channel tuning, plus an Enter button to confirm tuning.

text: How did the interface layout develop from IS1008b to IS1008c, and why was the numeric keypad placed lower than the volume and channel controls?
reference_answer: IS1008b called for few buttons and prominent controls for common functions. IS1008c placed volume and channel controls for thumb access and the numeric keypad lower down, citing more frequent use of volume and channel browsing than of the numeric keypad.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The interface should have few buttons, with frequently used controls made larger and placed strategically.

text: How was the essential-button requirement refined from ES2008b to ES2008c, and why were advanced functions assigned to a menu?
reference_answer: ES2008b required large, accessible buttons for essential functions. ES2008c specified power, volume, preset favourite-channel and menu buttons. Advanced functions were placed in an on-screen menu to keep the physical controls few and simple.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Use large, accessible buttons for essential functions.

text: From TS3003b to TS3003c, how did the plan for a docking station develop into a choice of power supply, and why was that source preferred to kinetic power?
reference_answer: TS3003b included a docking station in the design. In TS3003c the team selected a battery that could be recharged in that station, judging it just as suitable as kinetic power and much cheaper.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The remote control should include a docking station.

text: How did the plan for speech recognition develop from TS3005b to TS3005c, and why was a microphone planned?
reference_answer: In TS3005b, speech recognition was conditional on having enough manufacturing budget left. In TS3005c, a microphone was planned to enable that feature if implemented, with its placement on the remote discussed as a design detail.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Include speech recognition only if enough manufacturing budget remains.

text: From ES2014b to ES2014c, how was the lost-remote locator refined, and why was speech recognition limited to locating the device?
reference_answer: ES2014b selected a clap-activated locator. ES2014c specified recognising a recorded message and replying to help the user find the remote. Speech recognition served this locating function rather than television control because it was treated as a separate unit that replied to the user instead of sending television commands, allowing the simple circuit board to be retained.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Use a clap-activated locator to help users find a misplaced remote control.

text: How did the user-friendliness requirement become more specific from TS3011a to TS3011b, and what condition applied to the added feature?
reference_answer: TS3011a set the general goal of an original, trendy and user-friendly television remote. In TS3011b, complaints about losing the remote led the team to agree on a sound-based locating function to make it easier to find, provided it could be implemented within the budget. The technical solution was left for further investigation.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Develop an original, trendy and user-friendly television remote control.

text: How did the power plan change from ES2002c to ES2002d, and why?
reference_answer: ES2002c planned kinetic power together with a backup battery. ES2002d removed the kinetic source and kept battery power because of cost constraints.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Use kinetic power together with a backup battery.

text: How was the display plan made more specific from ES2002c to the final ES2002d design, and why was that arrangement used?
reference_answer: ES2002c opted against an LCD on the remote because of its cost and questionable need. The final ES2002d design specified navigation feedback on the television screen. Using the television to show the actions allowed the remote LCD and its associated electronics costs to be removed.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Do not include an LCD screen on the remote.

text: How was the case-material plan made more specific from TS3003c to the costed prototype in TS3003d, and why was that material used?
reference_answer: TS3003c planned interchangeable covers in wood or wood-effect and plastic versions. The prototype costed in TS3003d uses plastic, identified as the cheapest case material needed for that design.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Offer interchangeable case covers in wood or wood-effect and plastic versions.

text: How did the essential-button plan become more specific from ES2008c to ES2008d, and how was the count treated during costing?
reference_answer: ES2008c listed controls for power, volume, favourite channels and menu access. ES2008d fixed the physical total at six buttons, including power. During the cost review, the project manager retained six as a requirement while other costs were adjusted.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Include controls for power, volume, favourite channels and menu access.

text: How was ES2008b's requirement for a recognizable corporate image made concrete in ES2008d's colour design, and what prompted that specification?
reference_answer: ES2008b required the corporate image to be recognizable through the design, including company colours and slogan. In ES2008d the team specified a corporate-colour version with black buttons and a yellow exterior after noticing that the corporate colours had been overlooked, while retaining other colour options.
author: gm
superseded_answer: The remote's design must make the corporate image recognizable through the company colours and slogan.

text: How was the single-curved case planned in TS3003c carried into the TS3003d prototype, and why was that shape kept?
reference_answer: TS3003c selected a single-curved case to make the screen easier to view, especially for elderly users. TS3003d retained that shape in the plastic prototype despite its extra shaping cost, because the curve gave the display a prominent position on the remote.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Use a single-curved case so that the screen is easier to view.

text: How did the budget-dependent speech-recognition decision in TS3005b change by TS3005d, and why?
reference_answer: TS3005b agreed to include speech recognition only if enough money remained in the budget. In TS3005d the team explicitly dropped that feature together with its speaker during the cost-reduction redesign.
author: gm
superseded_answer: Include speech recognition only if enough money remains in the production budget.
